recommendations.regimenLabel: Emergency/supportive care (fluids, bisphosphonate, VTE prophylaxis); haematology-directed anti-myeloma therapy
steps: Manage emergencies: hypercalcaemia (fluids + bisphosphonate), AKI (hydration, stop nephrotoxins), cord compression, infection.
Bone disease: bisphosphonate (zoledronic acid) + analgesia ± radiotherapy/vertebroplasty.
Refer haematology — definitive therapy is combination anti-myeloma regimens ± autologous stem-cell transplant.
Anaemia support; VTE prophylaxis with immunomodulatory regimens; vaccination/infection prophylaxis.
Confirm with serum/urine electrophoresis, free light chains, marrow and imaging.

drugRefs.dose: IV volume repletion (e.g. 3–4 L/24 h if tolerated)
drugRefs.why: First-line for myeloma hypercalcaemia and cast-nephropathy AKI — restores volume, promotes calciuresis and renal clearance of light chains.

drugRefs.dose: 4 mg IV over ≥15 min (renal-adjusted), after rehydration
drugRefs.freq: monthly for bone disease; single dose for acute hypercalcaemia
drugRefs.why: Reduces skeletal events and pain and treats hypercalcaemia; dose-adjust for renal function and ensure dental review (ONJ risk).

drugRefs.dose: 75–100 mg PO once daily (LMWH if higher thrombotic risk)
drugRefs.why: Thalidomide/lenalidomide-based regimens are strongly prothrombotic; aspirin (or LMWH in high-risk patients) is standard thromboprophylaxis.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Plasma Cell Disorders
NICE NG35 — Myeloma: Diagnosis and Management

confirm: CRAB features — hyperCalcaemia, Renal impairment, Anaemia, Bone lesions/pain — with paraprotein and clonal marrow plasma cells.
